USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

A fixed elimination rate

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A toxicology teaching model describes removal of a hypothetical drug at a constant rate of 10 mg/hour while the amount falls from 200 mg to 100 mg. There is no further input. How much time does that decrease require in this zero-order range?

  1. 5 hours
  2. 20 hours
  3. 2 hours
  4. The time is independent of the initial amount for every zero-order drug
  5. 10 hours
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

10 hours

Removing 100 mg at 10 mg/hour takes 10 hours; the calculation uses a fixed amount rate.

Understanding the options

10 hours
Removing 100 mg at 10 mg/hour takes 10 hours; the calculation uses a fixed amount rate.
5 hours
Only 50 mg would be removed in five hours at the stated rate.
20 hours
Twenty hours would remove 200 mg if the same model remained valid.
2 hours
Only 20 mg would be removed in two hours.
The time is independent of the initial amount for every zero-order drug
The time to remove a specified fraction depends on the starting amount in zero-order kinetics.
